qualityObjective.en:
Provide a clean, sound, dry, level, properly profiled concrete substrate suitable for the specified floor finish system.
A large percentage of floor-finish failures originate in poor substrate preparation rather than the finish material itself.

authorityNote.en: The project drawings, devis, Plan Qualite, PIE/PRIE, approved procedures, professional instructions and CRT/Hydro-Quebec requirements govern. This playbook tells you how to systematically find, verify, document and close the quality requirements; it does not replace them.

text.en: Tile floor around drain does not maintain required slope.
Measure slope → identify affected area → remove/rebuild substrate or tile as approved → reinstall → verify drainage → document.
Vinyl flooring develops bubbles after installation.
Identify extent → verify substrate moisture/adhesive condition → determine approved repair → lift/rebond or replace as required → reinspect → document.
Coating pulls off during adhesion check.
Identify failed area → verify surface preparation/moisture → remove unsound coating → reprepare → reapply approved system → retest → close.

qualityObjective.en:
This module should branch by system because tile, resilient flooring and epoxy behave very differently.
TILE: Install tile with the correct product, layout, substrate preparation, bonding coverage, alignment, joint spacing, movement joints and finish.
RESILIENT FLOORING: Install resilient flooring over a properly prepared, dry, smooth substrate with correct adhesive, seams, layout and transitions.
EPOXY / FLOOR COATINGS: Apply the approved floor-coating system to a properly prepared substrate under acceptable environmental conditions at the required thickness and finish.

PRACTICAL EXAMPLE — FLOOR FINISH IN AN ELECTRICAL ROOM
Suppose epoxy floor coating is scheduled tomorrow.
You should not simply arrive when they're already rolling coating.
